findings.summary: 'In-place' is used in section 2 before section 3 defines it.
findings.evidence: Section 2: "In-place sorts use O(1) or O(log n) stack"; section 3: "In-place: no big auxiliary array"
findings.fix: Move the Sort Properties definitions (stable, in-place) before Cases and Space, or define in-place where it is first used.

findings.summary: The Big-O growth classes appear as a bare list of seven items, with no ordering cue, no meaning and no example for any class.
findings.evidence:
O(1)
O(log n)
O(n)
O(n log n)
O(n²)
O(2ⁿ)
O(n!)
findings.fix: Turn it into a table or a ranked line, e.g. 'Class | Name | Example' (O(1) constant: array index; O(log n): binary search; O(n log n): merge sort; O(n²): bubble sort). Also say it runs from fastest to slowest growth.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "optimisation", "average").
findings.evidence: Bubble optimisation: stop when a full pass makes no swap, giving O(n) best case on sorted input; worst/average O(n²), O(1) space, stable
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The bubble sort swap count is given as ~n²/2 with no case, but that is only the worst case.
findings.fix: Write 'up to ~n²/2 swaps (worst case; ~n²/4 on average)'. Either figure equals the number of inversions, which insertion sort also moves one shift at a time.

findings.summary: One bullet packs three separate heap sort steps, and the same steps also appear in the diagram.
findings.evidence: Build max-heap in O(n), then swap root with last and sift down
findings.fix: Drop the bullet or split it into 'Build max-heap: O(n)' and 'Repeat: swap root with last, shrink the heap, sift down'. Let the Build/Swap/Shrink/Sift diagram carry the process.

findings.summary: Search on answer is named with two examples but never shown, so the learner is not taught how to define the monotonic predicate and search on it.
findings.evidence: "Search on answer: binary search any monotonic predicate (min capacity, square root)"
findings.fix: Add a short worked example, such as integer square root: lo=0, hi=x, predicate mid*mid <= x, keep the best mid and move lo=mid+1 when true, otherwise hi=mid-1.
